slides.title: if Statements
slides.content: An if statement executes code only when a condition is true. It is the most basic way to make decisions in your program.

exercise.prompt: Complete the condition to check if score is at least 60.

slides.title: if-else Statements
slides.content: An if-else statement runs one block when the condition is true and another block when it is false.

slides.title: else if Chains
slides.content: Use else if to check multiple conditions in order. The first matching condition runs, and the rest are skipped.

slides.title: switch Statements
slides.content: A switch statement compares a single value against multiple cases. It is cleaner than long else if chains for exact matches.

slides.title: for Loops
slides.content: A for loop repeats a block of code a fixed number of times. You control the start, end, and step of the loop.

slides.title: while Loops
slides.content: A while loop repeats code while a condition stays true. Use it when you do not know how many iterations are needed.

slides.title: break and continue
slides.content: break stops a loop early, while continue skips the current iteration and jumps to the next one.

slides.title: foreach Loops with Collections
slides.content: A foreach loop iterates over every element in a collection, such as an array or list. It is the simplest way to process each item.

exercise.prompt: Use foreach to print each fruit from the array.
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: foreach
When run, your code should output: Apple, Banana
